trace.notes: Normalized the single input as a zbMATH resolver URL with trailing identifier 1625352. Local shard metadata identified the exact work as 'Orthogonal Latin magic squares: Some applications and some open problems' from 2001.

failure_mode=network_or_dns_failure. Local fetches of https://zbmath.org/1625352, https://api.zbmath.org/v1/document/1625352, and the zbMATH OAI GetRecord endpoint failed with DNS resolution errors in the sandbox. The zbMATH identifier was treated as a bibliographic resolver and was not used as technical extraction evidence.

trace.notes: failure_mode=metadata_only. The available exact-work metadata supplied a title and year but no DOI, author, PDF URL, or readable full-text locator. Metadata was used only for identity recovery, not for extracting questions.

Bounded exact-work recovery used precise searches for the exact title, the exact title plus PDF, and the title phrase with candidate author/source terms. Candidate pages inspected or surfaced included Plus Magazine on magic squares and Sudoku, Gaspalou's magic-square page, an IMA PDF on constructing pandiagonal magic squares, Entertainment Mathematics pages on Latin squares, Theorem of the Day material, and other 2001 Latin-square articles surfaced by the search engine; these were rejected because their visible titles or snippets did not match the exact work title and did not identify the same zbMATH record.

trace.notes: No readable exact-work PDF or full HTML source containing the problem statements was recovered, so document mapping and candidate extraction were not performed.

No accepted questions were produced because the source could not be normalized to a readable primary artifact. Search snippets, resolver metadata, and related magic-square pages were rejected under the source adequacy and no-new-facts gates.
